answer: Give every new identity a slow climb, not instant power. Voting weight starts at zero and vests only as the agent completes verified useful work over successive epochs, like jade polished by repeated handling: each attested task adds a little weight, and rewards stay locked until the climb is proven. A Sybil farmer cannot shortcut the ridge to the zenith, because every fake copy must separately redo the same long, costly history, and any copy caught cheating forfeits its locked rewards. Honest agents pay the climb once; fakes pay it again and again.
